annotation.title_clean: Humanitarian benefits of emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapon systems
annotation.title_en: Humanitarian benefits of emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapon systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United States of America (submitted to CCW Group of Governmental Experts)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts (CCW/GGE.1/2018/WP.4)
annotation.summary_en: US working paper to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts arguing that emerging technologies in lethal autonomous weapon systems can reduce civilian casualties, citing existing state practice such as self-destruct mechanisms, better situational awareness, precision targeting and automated engagement. It opposes stigmatizing or banning such technologies.
key_provisions_or_claims: Autonomy-related technologies can reduce civilian harm in armed conflict.
Five examples: self-destruct/deactivation, civilian awareness, effects assessment, automated targeting, reduced need for self-defense fires.
Cites DoD Directive 3000.09 on engagement termination or human input.
Precision-guided and sensor-based weapons reduce collateral damage.
States should encourage innovation rather than stigmatize or ban LAWS technologies.
